33417-later-poems.title: Later Poems
33417-later-poems.creator: MCCLELLAND & STEWART, Limited, TORONTO
33417-later-poems.description: A book by MCCLELLAND & STEWART, Limited, TORONTO. First of all, the poet, as thousands more of our young men of ambition and confidence have done, went early to the United States, and until recently, except for rare and brief visits to his old home down by the sea, has never returned to Canada--though for all that, I am able to state, on his own authority, he is still a Canadian citizen.

arxiv-2004-12344.title: Climate Adaptation: Reliably Predicting from Imbalanced Satellite Data
arxiv-2004-12344.creator: Ruchit Rawal, Prabhu Pradhan
arxiv-2004-12344.description: Abstract The utility of aerial imagery (Satellite, Drones) has become an invaluable information source for cross-disciplinary applications, especially for crisis management. Most of the mapping and tracking efforts are manual which is resource-intensive and often lead to delivery delays. Deep Learning methods have boosted the capacity of relief efforts via recognition, detection, and are now being used for non-trivial applications.

arxiv-2010-11575.title: Face Hallucination via Split-Attention in Split-Attention Network Thanks: ∗ * is the corresponding author (w906522992@gmail.com) CCS: Computing methodologies Image processing CCS: Computing methodologies Image representations CCS: Computing methodologies Appearance and texture representations
arxiv-2010-11575.creator: Tao Lu, Yuanzhi Wang ∗, Yanduo Zhang, Yu Wang, Wei Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Junjun Jiang
arxiv-2010-11575.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Tao Lu, Yuanzhi Wang ∗, Yanduo Zhang, Yu Wang, Wei Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Junjun Jiang. Recently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely employed to promote the face hallucination due to the ability to predict high-frequency details from a large number of samples. However, most of them fail to take into account the overall facial profile and fine texture details simultaneously, resulting in reduced naturalness and fidelity of the reconstructed face, and further impairing the performance of downstream tasks (e.g., face detection, facial recognition).

arxiv-2103-00419.title: A Multi-Scale Method for Distributed Convex Optimization with Constraints Journal: JOTA
arxiv-2103-00419.creator: Wei Ni, Xiaoli Wang
arxiv-2103-00419.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wei Ni, Xiaoli Wang. This paper proposes a multi-scale method to design a continuous-time distributed algorithm for constrained convex optimization problems by using multi-agents with Markov switched network dynamics and noisy inter-agent communications. Unlike most previous work which mainly puts emphasis on dealing with fixed network topology, this paper tackles the challenging problem of investigating the joint effects of stochastic networks and the inter-agent communication noises on the distributed optimization dynamics, which has not been systemically studied in the past literature.

arxiv-2107-03744.title: Analytic Tadpole Coefficients of One-loop Integrals
arxiv-2107-03744.creator: Bo Feng, Tingfei Li, Xiaodi Li
arxiv-2107-03744.description: Abstract One remaining problem of unitarity cut method for one-loop integral reduction is that tadpole coefficients can not be straightforward obtained through this way. In this paper, we reconsider the problem by applying differential operators over an auxiliary vector R R . Using differential operators, we establish the corresponding differential equations for tadpole coefficients at the first step.

arxiv-2204-05531.title: Assessment of sub-sampling schemes for compressive nano-FTIR imaging
arxiv-2204-05531.creator: Selma Metzner 1 , Bernd Kästner 1 , Manuel Marschall 1 , Gerd Wübbeler 1 , Stefan Wundrack 1 , Andrey Bakin 2 , Arne Hoehl 1 , Eckart Rühl 3 and Clemens Elster 1
arxiv-2204-05531.description: Abstract Nano-FTIR imaging is a powerful scanning-based technique at nanometer spatial resolution which combines Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). However, recording large spatial areas with nano-FTIR is limited by long measurement times due to its sequential data acquisition. Several mathematical approaches have been proposed to tackle this problem.

arxiv-2301-00316.title: Optimization Perspectives on Shellsort
arxiv-2301-00316.creator: Oscar Skean, Richard Ehrenborg, Jerzy W. Jaromczyk
arxiv-2301-00316.description: Abstract Shellsort is a sorting method that is attractive due to its simplicity, yet it takes effort to analyze its efficiency. The heart of the algorithm is the gap sequence chosen a priori and used during sorting. The selection of this gap sequence affects the efficiency of Shellsort, and thus drives both its theoretical and experimental analysis.

arxiv-2310-06301.title: Dynamical versus Bayesian Phase Transitions in a Toy Model of Superposition
arxiv-2310-06301.creator: Zhongtian Chen, Edmund Lau, Jake Mendel, Susan Wei, Daniel Murfet
arxiv-2310-06301.description: Abstract We investigate phase transitions in a Toy Model of Superposition (TMS) ( Elhage et al. 2022 ) using Singular Learning Theory (SLT). We derive a closed formula for the theoretical loss and, in the case of two hidden dimensions, discover that regular k k -gons are critical points.

arxiv-2404-16014.title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv-2404-16014.creator: Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Arthur Conmy, Lewis Smith, Tom Lieberum †, Vikrant Varma †, János Kramár, Rohin Shah, Neel Nanda
arxiv-2404-16014.description: Abstract Recent work has found that sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are an effective technique for unsupervised discovery of interpretable features in language models’ (LMs) activations, by finding sparse, linear reconstructions of LM activations. We introduce the Gated Sparse Autoencoder (Gated SAE), which achieves a Pareto improvement over training with prevailing methods.

arxiv-2411-17143.title: Topological simplicity of the group of automorphisms of the affine plane Thanks: The author gratefully acknowledges support by the Swiss National Science Foundation Grant “Birational transformations of higher dimensional varieties” 200020_214999
arxiv-2411-17143.creator: Jérémy Blanc
arxiv-2411-17143.description: Abstract . We prove that the group SAut k ​ ( 𝔸 2 ) \mathrm{SAut}_{\mathrm{k}}(\mathbb{A}^{2}) is simple as an algebraic group of infinite dimension, over any infinite field k \mathrm{k} , by proving that any closed normal subgroup is either trivial or the whole group. In higher dimension, we show that closed normal subgroups contain all tame automorphisms.

arxiv-2505-08394.title: Probability measures on families of partitions related to harmonic analysis on big wreath products
arxiv-2505-08394.creator: Eugene Strahov
arxiv-2505-08394.description: Abstract . We construct generalized regular representations of the wreath product of a compact group with the infinite symmetric group. The characters of these representations are determined by probability measures on families of partitions called the z z -measures for the wreath product of a compact group with the symmetric group in the present paper.

arxiv-2509-13619.title: Broadband femtosecond lasers enable efficient two-photon excitation of the ultranarrow linewidth singlet 1s2s state in helium
arxiv-2509-13619.creator: Shashank Kumar, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Niranjan Shivaram
arxiv-2509-13619.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shashank Kumar, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Niranjan Shivaram. We propose a broadband, femtosecond two-photon excitation scheme for efficient population transfer to the ultra-narrow linewidth 1 ​ s ​ 2 ​ s 1 ​ S 0 1s2s\ ^{1}S_{0} metastable state in helium. Using 120 120 nm vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) femtosecond laser pulses, we theoretically demonstrate that a direct two-photon excitation process can achieve a population transfer efficiency of 25–30%, even when photoionization losses are included.

arxiv-2510-21818.title: Vertex and front-tracking methods for the modeling of microstructure evolution at the solid state: a brief review
arxiv-2510-21818.creator: Marc Bernacki
arxiv-2510-21818.description: Abstract In mesoscopic scale microstructure evolution modeling, two primary numerical frameworks are used: Front-Capturing (FC) and Front-Tracking (FT) ones. FC models, like phase-field or level-set methods, indirectly define interfaces by tracking field variable changes. On the contrary, FT models explicitly define interfaces using interconnected segments or surfaces.

britannica-1911-fermat-pierre-de.title: Fermat, Pierre de (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-fermat-pierre-de.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-fermat-pierre-de.description: Article 'Fermat, Pierre de' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Fermat was for some time councillor for the parliament of Toulouse, and in the discharge of the duties of that office he was distinguished both for legal knowledge and for strict integrity of conduct. Though the sciences were the principal objects of his private studies, he was also an accomplished general scholar and an excellent linguist.

pmc-10738002.title: COMPARING SELF-REPORTED MEASURES OF SUBJECTIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE
pmc-10738002.creator: Benjamin Olivari, John Omura, John Shean, Lisa McGuire
pmc-10738002.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Symptoms of subjective cognitive decline (SCD) can be early indicators of possible future dementia. Estimates of self-reported SCD prevalence are available from various data sources including the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System’s (BRFSS) current Cognitive Decline Optional Module. Recent revisions to the Module were proposed based on input from subject matter experts, including reducing introductory phrasing and refining question and response options. It is unknown how these changes may impact estimates of SCD prevalence.

pmc-11331031.title: Intra‐flap recurrence of an oral squamous cell carcinoma after curative resection and reconstruction with a free flap
pmc-11331031.creator: Paris Liokatis, Ioanna Liokati, Florian Nepomuk Fegg, Ina Dewenter, Gerson Mast, Sven Otto, Katharina Theresa Obermeier
pmc-11331031.description: Key Clinical MessageIntra‐flap recurrence after reconstruction is a possible complication in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) after curative resection and reconstruction with a free flap.AbstractThis case report describes an intra‐flap recurrence after tumor resection and reconstruction with a latissimus dorsi flap due to OSCC.

pmc-11431881.title: The Role of Risk Factors for the Progression of Patients with T1b-T2 Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma (PC) during Long-Term Follow-Up
pmc-11431881.creator: Andrea Marongiu, Susanna Nuvoli, Andrea De Vito, Antonio Mura, Sonia Vargiu, Angela Spanu, Giuseppe Madeddu, Michael Kreissl
pmc-11431881.description: Background/Objectives: Recurrence prediction for patients with PC and tumor sizes ranging between 1 and 4 cm, classified as T1b and T2, remains a controversial problem. We evaluated which risk factors, identified during the primary tumor surgery, might play a prognostic role in predicting disease progression.

pmc-12478113.title: M1-like macrophages regulate T cell infiltration in colorectal cancer through P2X4 receptor
pmc-12478113.creator: Kun Zhou, Xintian Zhang, Yu Liang, Han Yao, Yichao Hou, Xingming Zhang, Leilei Du, Wenfeng Wang, Jianhua Wang, Xiangjun Meng
pmc-12478113.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryAlthough tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a critical immunomodulatory role in colorectal cancer (CRC), the mechanisms underlying their polarization remain unclear. This study identifies the P2X4 receptor (P2X4R) as a crucial mediator of M1-like polarization. During TAM induction in a controlled in vitro system using CRC cell-conditioned medium, we observed P2X4R-mediated calcium influx and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction through immunofluorescence and mitochondrial assays. This dysfunction led to mitochondrial DNA release and subsequent activation of the cGAS-STING-IFNB1 pathway, driving M1-like polarization of TAMs.

pmc-13393349.title: Recurrence after healing in pyoderma gangrenosum: a prospective registry-based cohort study
pmc-13393349.creator: Jordan Gillespie, Jaclyn Roland-McGowan, Katelyn Downey, Emile Latour, Alex G Ortega-Loayza
pmc-13393349.description: SummaryBackgroundPyoderma gangrenosum is a rare neutrophilic dermatosis with potential for relapse after healing, yet recurrence in real-world settings remains unknown. We aimed to evaluate recurrence patterns to inform clinical practice and future research.MethodsData were abstracted from a uniquely, prospectively maintained pyoderma gangrenosum registry.

pmc-13398155.title: Unraveling the Individualized Shared and Distinct Dynamic Functional Connectivity in Idiopathic Autism Spectrum Disorder and Fragile X Syndrome
pmc-13398155.creator: Boli Pan, Junbo Wang, Danyong Feng, Yiting Zhu, Ning Tang, Dongyun Li, Qiong Xu, Rihui Li
pmc-13398155.description: AimsAutism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), a neurodevelopmental disorder, and Fragile X Syndrome (FXS), an X chromosome‐linked hereditary neurodevelopmental disorder, exhibit overlapping phenotypes like social impairment and stereotyped behaviors. Previous studies have predominantly explored the functional network characteristics of either FXS or ASD. However, the shared and distinct dynamic neural circuitry underlying both disorders remains unclear, impeding personalized treatment.

pmc-13502420.title: Mechanisms and situational patterns of anterior cruciate ligament injuries in professional women's football (soccer): A systematic video analysis across 25 leagues (2022–2024)
pmc-13502420.creator: Wyatt Hampstead, Ric Lovell, Matthew Whalan, Lionel Chia, Joshua Bonney, Bradley Wakefield, Vanessa Crespin, Evangelos Pappas
pmc-13502420.description: PurposesTo identify and describe the biomechanical characteristics and football‐specific contextual factors associated with anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries in professional women's football.MethodsA media‐based prospective cross‐sectional study identified 247 ACL injuries across international matches and 25 national women's leagues (tiers 3–5) between 2022 and 2024 using a validated media‐based surveillance approach.

pmc-13647509.title: Integrin-β1/FAK signaling is involved in electrical stimulation to prevent disuse muscular atrophy induced by tail suspension in mice
pmc-13647509.creator: Yizheng Huang, Jia He, Xiaofeng Duan, Jiahao Chen, Zilong Zhao, Hao Hu
pmc-13647509.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundElectrical stimulation is a widely used method for preventing and treating disuse muscle atrophy; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely examined. Integrins, a class of transmembrane cell adhesion receptors, are considered primary mechanosensors involved in load-induced muscle growth. However, no previous studies have demonstrated whether integrin β1 and its downstream FAK signaling pathway are involved in the prevention of disuse muscle atrophy via electrical stimulation.
